subject: general
question: Andal was one of the most famous women ________ saints.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alvar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Andal** was one of the twelve Alvars, who were Tamil poet-saints devoted to Lord Vishnu in the Bhakti tradition of South India.
 
• She is the only female among the Alvars and is highly revered for her devotional poetry and deep love for Lord Vishnu.
 
• Andal is best known for her two works, **Tiruppavai** and **Nachiyar Tirumozhi**, which are considered significant contributions to Tamil devotional literature.
 
• Her devotion to Lord Vishnu is celebrated during the **Margazhi month** (December-January), especially in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Andal's compositions reflect themes of longing, love, and surrender to the divine, embodying the essence of the Bhakti movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alvars:**

 
 
• The Alvars were a group of 12 Tamil poet-saints who lived between the 6th and 9th centuries CE and were devoted to Lord Vishnu.
 
• Their hymns, collectively known as the **Nalayira Divya Prabandham**, are considered sacred texts in the Vaishnavite tradition.
 
• The Alvars played a significant role in propagating the Bhakti movement in South India.
 
 
 
• **Tiruppavai:**
 
 
• It is a collection of 30 devotional hymns composed by Andal in praise of Lord Vishnu.
 
• The Tiruppavai is recited daily during the Margazhi month and holds a central place in Tamil Vaishnavite tradition.
 
 
 
• **Nachiyar Tirumozhi:**
 
 
• This is another literary work of Andal that expresses her deep love and yearning for union with Lord Vishnu.
 
• It comprises 143 verses and is part of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham.
 
 
 
• **Bhakti Movement:**
 
 
• The Bhakti movement emphasized devotion and surrender to a personal deity, cutting across social and caste barriers.
 
• The Alvars and Nayanars (devotees of Shiva) were among the earliest proponents of the Bhakti tradition in South India.
